# Daily Dashboard V0.5.10

Windows display locking now has recovery paths when the saved monitor is missing, reconfigured or cannot be restored.

- Startup/relaunch immediately offers a native recovery prompt when the saved display cannot be used. Choose Yes to remove the binding and open on the main screen, or No to keep waiting.
- A running Dashboard offers recovery after 10 seconds of failed restoration. Brief disconnects recover automatically, without repeated prompts during one outage.
- Recovery restores minimized/maximized windows before placing them on an available display, so Windows cannot subsequently restore an old offscreen position. Reconnecting restores a minimized window and reapplies borderless bounds without retaining a stale native fullscreen monitor. Placement is checked before marking recovery successful.
- `--unlock-display` clears the saved binding and opens a normal window in the main monitor's work area. `--reset-display-lock` is an alias. Other settings are preserved.
- Launch commands reach the already-running Windows instance. `--keep-display-lock` explicitly waits without automatic prompts; a normal relaunch or tray Show command offers recovery again.
- The installer adds **Daily Dashboard - Recover display** to the Windows Start menu. Tray recovery remains available.
- Unlock releases confinement even if saving preferences fails, reports that failure and leaves an unreadable settings file intact. Late prompt responses cannot undo a newer binding change.

From PowerShell in the installation folder:

```powershell
.\V0.5.10_Daily-Dashboard.exe --unlock-display
```

[Recovery guide and command reference](https://github.com/BananaAficionado/DailyDashboard/blob/main/docs/dedicated-display.md).

These native changes are Windows-only; macOS keeps its existing window behaviour. Close older Dashboard versions before upgrading. A genuinely unresponsive Windows process must be ended in Task Manager before relaunching unlocked.

## Verification

Frontend checks and production build pass. Native recovery tests cover launch precedence, outage timing, duplicate prompts and fitting recovery windows at high DPI/negative coordinates. All 17 macOS native tests and Windows cross-compilation (including test code) pass. Browser checks pass for monitor Settings at all 19 documented display/scaling configurations and 120 layout cases covering all six widgets at four sizes across five representative displays. Windows CI builds the installer and executes the full native suite.

Physical unplug/replug, dock/driver resets and the native prompt on your GPU/monitor configuration still require Windows hardware testing.
